# ACS Clinical Compass
## Acute Coronary Syndrome Insurance Authorization Guide

[Button] Back to Assessment (navigates to /acs)

---

## Procedure Codes (CPT)

Each entry: CPT code badge, RVU badge, description, Device/Access line, 'Included in this code (do NOT bill separately):' checklist, and an italic note.

### CPT 92928 — RVU 11.21
Percutaneous transcatheter placement of intracoronary stent(s), with coronary angioplasty when performed; single major coronary artery or branch
Device/Access: Intracoronary stent(s), balloon catheter | Percutaneous (e.g., femoral, radial artery)
Included in this code (do NOT bill separately):
- Vascular access and closure
- Catheter placement and manipulation
- Angiography and imaging supervision/interpretation
- Angioplasty (if performed)
- Stent deployment
Note: Used for single lesion in a major coronary artery or its branches.

### CPT 92933 — RVU 12.29
Percutaneous transcatheter placement of intracoronary stent(s), with coronary atherectomy and angioplasty when performed; single major coronary artery or branch
Device/Access: Intracoronary stent(s), atherectomy device, balloon catheter | Percutaneous (e.g., femoral, radial artery)
Included in this code (do NOT bill separately):
- Vascular access and closure
- Catheter placement and manipulation
- Angiography and imaging supervision/interpretation
- Atherectomy
- Angioplasty (if performed)
- Stent deployment
Note: Used for single lesion in a major coronary artery or its branches, including atherectomy.

### CPT 92937 — RVU 11.50 (Estimated RVU, similar to native vessel PCI)
Percutaneous transluminal revascularization of or through coronary artery bypass graft (internal mammary, free arterial, venous), any combination of atherectomy, angioplasty, and/or stent placement; single major coronary artery or branch
Device/Access: Intracoronary stent(s), atherectomy device, balloon catheter | Percutaneous (e.g., femoral, radial artery)
Included in this code (do NOT bill separately):
- Vascular access and closure
- Catheter placement and manipulation
- Angiography and imaging supervision/interpretation
- Atherectomy (if performed)
- Angioplasty (if performed)
- Stent deployment
Note: Used for revascularization of a single major coronary artery or its branches through a bypass graft.

### CPT 92941 — RVU 15.00 (Estimated RVU for emergent PCI in AMI)
Percutaneous transluminal revascularization of acute total/subtotal occlusion of coronary artery or coronary artery bypass graft, any combination of atherectomy, angioplasty, and/or stent placement; with or without thrombectomy, in an acute myocardial infarction; single major coronary artery or coronary artery bypass graft
Device/Access: Intracoronary stent(s), atherectomy device, balloon catheter, thrombectomy device | Percutaneous (e.g., femoral, radial artery)
Included in this code (do NOT bill separately):
- Vascular access and closure
- Catheter placement and manipulation
- Angiography and imaging supervision/interpretation
- Atherectomy (if performed)
- Angioplasty (if performed)
- Stent deployment
- Thrombectomy (if performed)
Note: Emergent revascularization for acute myocardial infarction (AMI) due to total/subtotal occlusion.

### CPT 92943 — RVU 16.50 (Estimated RVU for complex CTO PCI)
Percutaneous transluminal revascularization of chronic total occlusion of coronary artery or coronary artery bypass graft, any combination of atherectomy, angioplasty, and/or stent placement; with or without thrombectomy, in a chronic total occlusion; single major coronary artery or coronary artery bypass graft
Device/Access: Intracoronary stent(s), atherectomy device, balloon catheter, thrombectomy device | Percutaneous (e.g., femoral, radial artery)
Included in this code (do NOT bill separately):
- Vascular access and closure
- Catheter placement and manipulation
- Angiography and imaging supervision/interpretation
- Atherectomy (if performed)
- Angioplasty (if performed)
- Stent deployment
- Thrombectomy (if performed)
Note: Complex revascularization for chronic total occlusion (CTO) of a coronary artery or bypass graft.

---

## ICD-10 Diagnosis Codes

Each entry shows code badge, description, notes, and a 'Primary' badge when required.

- I21.0 (Primary) — ST elevation (STEMI) myocardial infarction of anterior wall. Requires immediate intervention. Primary diagnosis for anterior STEMI.
- I21.1 (Primary) — ST elevation (STEMI) myocardial infarction of inferior wall. Requires immediate intervention. Primary diagnosis for inferior STEMI.
- I21.2 (Primary) — ST elevation (STEMI) myocardial infarction of other sites. Requires immediate intervention. Primary diagnosis for other STEMI locations.
- I21.3 (Primary) — ST elevation (STEMI) myocardial infarction of unspecified site. Requires immediate intervention. Primary diagnosis for unspecified STEMI.
- I21.4 (Primary) — Non-ST elevation (NSTEMI) myocardial infarction. Often requires urgent intervention. Primary diagnosis for NSTEMI.
- I22.0 — Subsequent ST elevation (STEMI) myocardial infarction of anterior wall. Used for a new STEMI occurring within 28 days of a previous MI. Specify site.
- I22.1 — Subsequent ST elevation (STEMI) myocardial infarction of inferior wall. Used for a new STEMI occurring within 28 days of a previous MI. Specify site.
- I25.10 — Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery without angina pectoris. Used for underlying coronary artery disease. Not a primary diagnosis for acute event.

---

## Payer-Specific Authorization Requirements

Tabs: Medicare | Medicaid | Private Insurance

### Medicare
Status badges: No Prior Auth (FFS) | Covered for Medically Necessary Services
Prior Auth Note: Generally, Medicare does not require prior authorization for emergent PCI procedures in the setting of acute myocardial infarction. However, documentation must clearly support medical necessity.
Overview: Medicare covers percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for beneficiaries with acute coronary syndromes (ACS) when performed in accordance with established clinical guidelines and medical necessity criteria. Coverage typically includes diagnostic catheterization, angioplasty, stenting, and atherectomy when indicated.

Coverage Criteria — Acute Myocardial Infarction (AMI):
- Clinical symptoms consistent with AMI (e.g., chest pain, shortness of breath)
- ECG changes indicative of STEMI or high-risk NSTEMI
- Elevated cardiac biomarkers (e.g., troponin, CK-MB)
- Angiographic evidence of significant coronary artery stenosis or occlusion amenable to PCI
Coverage Criteria — Unstable Angina / NSTEMI (Non-Emergent):
- Recurrent angina at rest or with minimal exertion
- Ischemic changes on ECG (e.g., ST depression, T-wave inversion)
- Positive stress test or other non-invasive evidence of ischemia
- Angiographic evidence of significant coronary artery stenosis amenable to PCI after medical management failure

Required Documentation — Clinical Records:
- Detailed history and physical examination
- Emergency department notes (if applicable)
- Serial ECGs
- Cardiac biomarker trends
- Consultation reports (Cardiology, Interventional Cardiology)
Required Documentation — Procedure Documentation:
- Operative report detailing procedure, findings, and devices used
- Angiographic images and interpretation
- Hemodynamic data
- Device implant cards (for stents)

Submission Process:
1. Submit claims using appropriate CPT and ICD-10 codes.
2. Ensure all documentation supporting medical necessity is available upon request.
3. For emergent cases, use appropriate modifiers (e.g., -STAT) if applicable to indicate urgency.

Common Denial Reasons:
- Lack of medical necessity documentation
- Inadequate angiographic evidence of significant stenosis
- PCI performed for stable angina without prior medical management failure (for non-emergent cases)
- Incorrect coding or modifier usage

Known Payer Policies:
| Payer | Status | Notes |
| CMS | Covered | National Coverage Determinations (NCDs) and Local Coverage Determinations (LCDs) apply. Refer to specific MAC policies. |

Reimbursement Note: Reimbursement for PCI procedures is typically based on DRG for inpatient stays and APC for outpatient services. Specific payment rates vary by geographic location and facility type.

Authorization Tips:
- Clearly document the patient's clinical presentation, especially for emergent cases.
- Ensure all diagnostic findings (ECG, biomarkers, angiography) are thoroughly documented and support the intervention.
- For non-emergent PCI, document prior medical management and its failure.

### Medicaid
Status badges: Prior Auth Required | Covered with Prior Authorization
Prior Auth Note: Prior authorization is generally required for all non-emergent PCI procedures. Emergent cases may be exempt but require retrospective review and robust documentation.
Overview: Medicaid programs cover PCI for ACS patients, but policies vary significantly by state. Most states require prior authorization for elective procedures and may have specific criteria for emergent interventions. Documentation of medical necessity is paramount.

Coverage Criteria — Acute Myocardial Infarction (AMI):
- Clinical presentation consistent with AMI
- ECG evidence of STEMI or high-risk NSTEMI
- Elevated cardiac biomarkers
- Angiographic evidence of significant coronary lesion requiring intervention
Coverage Criteria — Non-Emergent PCI (e.g., Unstable Angina):
- Documented failure of optimal medical therapy
- Objective evidence of myocardial ischemia (e.g., stress test, FFR)
- Significant coronary stenosis (typically >70% in major epicardial vessel or >50% in left main) on angiography
- Symptoms refractory to medical management

Required Documentation — Authorization Request:
- Completed prior authorization form
- Clinical notes, including H&P, ED notes, cardiology consults
- ECG reports and cardiac biomarker results
- Angiography report and images
- Documentation of failed medical therapy (for non-emergent cases)
Required Documentation — Procedure Documentation:
- Operative report
- Device implant information

Submission Process:
1. Obtain prior authorization before non-emergent procedures.
2. Submit claims with authorization number.
3. Ensure all medical records are readily available for post-service review.

Common Denial Reasons:
- Lack of prior authorization
- Insufficient documentation of medical necessity
- Failure to meet state-specific coverage criteria
- Incomplete or illegible medical records

Known Payer Policies:
| Payer | Status | Notes |
| State Medicaid (e.g., California Medi-Cal) | Covered with PA | Specific guidelines for emergent vs. elective PCI. Requires robust documentation. |

Reimbursement Note: Medicaid reimbursement rates are generally lower than Medicare or private payers and vary by state. Providers should be aware of state-specific fee schedules.

Authorization Tips:
- Verify state-specific Medicaid policies for PCI and prior authorization requirements.
- Maintain meticulous documentation, especially for emergent cases that bypass initial authorization.
- Consider peer-to-peer review for complex cases or initial denials.

### Private Insurance
Status badges: Prior Auth Required | Covered with Prior Authorization
Prior Auth Note: Prior authorization is almost always required for all PCI procedures, both emergent and elective. Retrospective authorization may be granted for true emergencies.
Overview: Private insurance plans typically cover PCI for ACS, but coverage criteria and prior authorization requirements can vary widely by plan and insurer. It is crucial to verify benefits and obtain authorization before any elective procedure.

Coverage Criteria — Acute Myocardial Infarction (AMI):
- Diagnosis of STEMI or high-risk NSTEMI
- Clinical instability or ongoing ischemia
- Angiographic findings consistent with acute coronary occlusion or severe stenosis requiring urgent intervention
Coverage Criteria — Elective PCI (e.g., Stable Angina, NSTEMI after stabilization):
- Documented symptoms of angina or anginal equivalents
- Objective evidence of moderate to severe ischemia on non-invasive testing (e.g., stress test, nuclear scan)
- Significant coronary stenosis (e.g., >70% in major epicardial vessel, >50% in left main) with corresponding ischemia
- Failure of optimal medical therapy to control symptoms or improve prognosis

Required Documentation — Authorization Request:
- Completed prior authorization form with clinical rationale
- All relevant medical records (H&P, ED notes, consults, ECGs, labs)
- Non-invasive test results (stress test, echo, nuclear)
- Angiography report and images
- Documentation of medical therapy and its efficacy/failure
Required Documentation — Procedure Documentation:
- Operative report
- Device implant information

Submission Process:
1. Submit prior authorization request well in advance for elective procedures.
2. Follow up on authorization status regularly.
3. Submit claims with the approved authorization number.
4. Be prepared for potential peer-to-peer reviews or appeals.

Common Denial Reasons:
- Lack of prior authorization
- Insufficient medical necessity (e.g., PCI for non-ischemic lesions)
- Failure to meet plan-specific criteria (e.g., stenosis severity, symptom burden)
- Inadequate trial of medical therapy
- Documentation discrepancies

Known Payer Policies:
| Payer | Status | Notes |
| Blue Cross Blue Shield | Covered with PA | Follows ACC/AHA guidelines, but may have stricter criteria for elective PCI. |
| UnitedHealthcare | Covered with PA | Requires detailed clinical documentation and often a trial of medical therapy for stable CAD. |
| Aetna | Covered with PA | Emphasizes appropriate use criteria and evidence-based guidelines for revascularization. |

Reimbursement Note: Reimbursement rates are negotiated between providers and individual private insurance companies. Out-of-network services may have different coverage and patient cost-sharing.

Authorization Tips:
- Always verify patient's benefits and specific plan requirements before scheduling elective PCI.
- Document all conservative management attempts and their outcomes.
- Utilize peer-to-peer reviews as an opportunity to advocate for the patient and provide additional clinical context.
- Be aware of specific payer policies regarding appropriate use criteria for revascularization.
